newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala says Germany helped in Nestle arrest.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala says Germany helped in Nestle arrest.

text.p: Guatemalan officials said on Thursday Germany had helped in a drug trafficking investigation that led to the arrest of the Swiss local manager of food and beverage giant Nestle SA and three others.

"We have relied on the help of German authorities to accumulate different information that has helped us deal a blow to the drug trafficking network between Guatemala and Europe," Deputy Interior Minister Salvador Gandara, told reporters.
Nestle said on Thursday it had no reason to doubt the integrity of Andreas Haenggi, who was arrested and accused of drug trafficking this week with his son Nicolas.
In Zurich, Nestle said Haenggi, 60, had been head of its foodstuffs factory in the city of Antigua, Guatemala, since 1993 and had worked for the company for 20 years.

The two Swiss were arrested along with the Guatemalan chief of police in Antigua, Jose Luis Sebadua Salazar, and another foreigner, Silvino Geovanelli, following the arrest in Germany of two German citizens, Guatemalan officials said.

Guatemala's Department of Anti-Narcotics Operations said the two Germans, Harmut Zersch and Dieter Chomsi, were caught delivering a cocaine shipment to Europe, and they told German authorities they had links to the two Swiss men.
Officials said the alleged drug ring used a plant export business as a front to ship cocaine from Colombia to Europe, and the Haenggis allegedly helped.
The suspects were in custody in a Guatemala City jail pending formal charges.
